Title: "Context Subgraph Enrichment for Multi-hop KGQA: An Ablation Study"

Research question: same as U003.

Hypothesis: Enriching target triples with local context subgraphs from the same source passage improves Hits@1 on multi-hop QA benchmarks compared to training on isolated triples alone.

Proposed method: Fine-tune a language model (e.g., BERT-base) on a KGQA dataset (e.g., MetaQA) under two conditions: (1) baseline: only target triple (head, relation, tail) as input; (2) method: target triple plus additional triples extracted from the same source passage (using OpenIE or dependency parsing to extract triples) concatenated or structured as a subgraph input (e.g., via textualization or graph neural network). Optionally include adaptive repair loop and RL transfer later, but for this experiment focus on context enrichment.

Baselines: Triple-only fine-tuning (same LM architecture), possibly also existing models like TransferNet, Rce-KGQA as stronger baselines.

Datasets: MetaQA (1-hop,2-hop,3-hop) or WebQuestionsSP-tiny.

Workloads: multi-hop QA.

Hardware: GPU (e.g., RTX 3090) or similar.

Software environment: PyTorch, Transformers library.

Metrics: Hits@1, Exact Match, F1.

Ablations: vary amount of context (e.g., 1-hop vs 2-hop context), different triple extraction methods (OpenIE vs dependency), different ways to encode subgraph (concatenation vs GNN).

Controls: same random seed, same preprocessing, same training hyperparameters except for input.

Confounders addressed: control for KG incompleteness by using a fixed KG (e.g., the one provided with MetaQA); ensure that the extracted triples are from the same passage used to generate the QA pair.

Expected outcomes: The method should yield higher Hits@1 than baseline, especially on 2-hop and 3-hop questions.

Failure conditions: If method does not outperform baseline by a statistically significant margin (e.g., p<0.05) on 2-hop or 3-hop Hits@1, hypothesis is falsified.

Reproducibility notes: Provide code, data splits, random seeds.

Related paper ids: we can include arxiv:2110.12679 (Relational Chain Reasoning) as a related work, and maybe doi:10.20944/preprints202505.1992.v1 (SG-RAG MOT) for subgraph context.
